speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me understand your condition better, how long have these symptoms been occurring?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST IMAGES: Bladder_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific_Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None; Bladder_Ultrasound: Postvoid_Residual_Urine 25 mL.

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis is clean of infection, and your ultrasound shows normal bladder emptying. Given your history of chronic discomfort, does the pain improve or worsen when you touch the area directly? Also, do you notice any blood in your urine at any time?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The relief of pain upon voiding and the presence of dyspareunia are highly suggestive of a bladder condition. Have you noticed any changes in the texture or consistency of the urine, and do you experience any pain in your lower back or hips?

REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture
REQUEST TEST: Urine_Cytology

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urine_Culture: No significant growth; Urine_Cytology: Negative for malignant cells.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative culture and cytology rule out infection and cancer. To further evaluate your chronic pelvic pain and frequency, I need to know if you experience pain deep inside your pelvis or specifically during ovulation, and have you had any history of sexually transmitted infections?

REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Exam
REQUEST TEST: CT_Pelvis_with_Cystogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_Exam: Inspection shows no external lesions, vaginal discharge, or obvious masses. Cervix appears normal upon speculum examination. Bimanual examination reveals normal uterus and adnexa, with discomfort noted on palpation of the bladder region. CT_Pelvis_with_Cystogram: Not included in provided data; NORMAL READINGS for available imaging.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pelvic exam confirms localized bladder tenderness without gynecological or infectious causes, and your imaging is normal. Have you noticed any microscopic blood in your urine despite the clear appearance, and does the discomfort persist even when your bladder is completely empty?

speaker: Doctor
text:
I have noted your response regarding the intercourse. Given the history of dyspareunia, suprapubic pain relieved by voiding, sterile urine, and normal imaging, do you have a history of interstitial cystitis or endometriosis, and does the pain specifically localize to the bladder area?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome
